messages:
mira: Kickoff: bringing up osmium14b quant int4 on dedicated-small for eval. Seeing intermittent OOMs and weird p95 spikes when workload contains long generations (>600 tokens).
raj: Can you share the canary config? microbatch, prefetch, max_new_tokens?
mira: Config: microbatch=1, batch=6, prefetch_window=160, prefetch_padding=0, max_new_tokens=1024 (temp for longform tests).
su: High prefetch_window + large max_new_tokens is a red flag. Quantized weights + slab allocator will fragment. Any stderr from the worker?
mira: Paste of the last trace: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while attempting to allocate 1.5 GiB
Backtrace: runtime/allocator.cc:198
Note: slot_allocator fragmentation: free_contig=768MB total_free=2.4GB
Timeline: prefetch->kv_prefetch->attn_kv_alloc->decode```
ben: That free_contig vs total_free confirms fragmentation. Two approaches: 1) lower prefetch_window + add prefetch_padding to reduce tight contiguous requests, 2) introduce a small kv-compact step before large alloc. Also consider soft microbatching (allow microbatch grow to fit).
mira: Quick repro: `./run_canary.sh --model osmium14b --quant int4 --prefetch 160 --max_new 1024` yields ~1 OOM / 120 requests. With prefetch=48 and max_new=512 OOMs disappear.
raj: For onboarding policy we should set conservative defaults for new int4 variants: max_new_tokens=512, prefetch_window<=64, prefetch_padding=32. Put this behind a per-model flag until we validate quality tradeoffs.
eva: Filed ticket ML-1499: "osmium14b-int4: conservative runtime defaults + kv-compact experiment".
deploy-bot: :rocket: rolling canary (osmium14b-int4) -> pool-dedicated-small-2
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary pod ready (v2026-03-24-int4-kvcompact-exp)
ben: I'll prototype kv-compact: on allocation failure, attempt to compact slabs for up to 200ms then retry allocation; if still failing, soft-evict least-recent-kv pages (up to 20%). Will run microbench.
su: Also run a quality sweep with the conservative defaults; sometimes lowering max_new truncates references and can change ROUGE/BERTScore. We'll run summarization + longform QA.
mira: Plan: (1) roll canary with conservative defaults, (2) run 10k request sweep with metrics: p95, p50, OOM count, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, cost/tokens, (3) if OOMs gone and quality delta <= 2 pts, promote.
raj: Add a runtime flag `model_config.prefetch_strategy=adaptive` that scales window = min(128, base + context/8) and caps contiguous allocations. That could mitigate fragmentation for variable-length requests.
ben: On it. I'll land kv-compact PR and bench against canary. If it regresses perf, we'll gate behind feature flag.
mira: Thanks team. Will post the sweep artifact link when done: s3://redwood-bench/osmium14b/int4/rollout-2026-03-24. Short term: keeping production default for int4 conservative. :thumbsup:
